hero.title: G7 Moves to Release 100 Million Barrels as Global Energy Crisis Deepens
hero.description: The G7 has agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of crude oil and refined fuel from emergency reserves over four months as energy prices remain under pressure. France, Europe, the UK, USA, Canada, Asia, Africa and Nigeria are also in focus.

featured.title: G7 Releases Emergency Oil and Fuel Reserves as Energy Prices Surge
featured.content: G7 countries have agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of crude oil and refined fuel from emergency reserves over the next four months. The plan includes a substantial front-loaded release of diesel during the first 20 days. The coordinated action comes as geopolitical conflict and disrupted supply routes push fuel prices higher. The measure is intended to increase market supply and reduce short-term pressure, although emergency stock releases cannot by themselves resolve the underlying supply disruptions.

articles.title: G7 Agrees Emergency Release of 100 Million Barrels
articles.content: The Group of Seven has agreed to release up to 100 million barrels of crude oil and refined fuel from emergency reserves over four months. A substantial portion of the initial release will focus on diesel during the first 20 days. The decision follows rising fuel prices and continued disruption to global energy supply routes. The International Energy Agency is coordinating the broader emergency response.

articles.title: France Student Protests Spread Across More Than 1,000 Schools
articles.content: A nationwide student protest movement in France has expanded rapidly, with more than 1,000 schools affected. Students have raised concerns about teacher shortages, overcrowded classrooms, poor facilities and education conditions. Some demonstrations have involved fires, clashes with police and arrests. Authorities have said peaceful protest is legitimate while condemning violence and damage to public property. The situation remains developing.

articles.title: Europe Faces Continued Energy and Inflation Pressure
articles.content: European households and businesses remain exposed to high energy costs as global fuel markets remain tight. The G7 emergency reserve release is intended partly to ease pressure on international fuel markets. Energy prices can affect transport, heating, electricity, manufacturing and food costs, keeping inflation and energy security high on the European policy agenda.

articles.title: UK Economy Grows 0.5% in Second Quarter
articles.content: The UK economy grew by 0.5% between April and June 2026, according to revised Office for National Statistics figures, compared with the previous estimate of 0.4%. Business investment and household disposable income also showed stronger figures during the quarter. However, higher energy costs and inflation remain important challenges for households and businesses.

articles.title: US Households Face Continued Energy and Cost Pressures
articles.content: Fuel prices and the wider cost of living remain important economic issues in the United States as global energy supplies remain under pressure. A recent AP-NORC poll found that 65% of surveyed US adults blamed President Donald Trump's policies for persistently high costs. That is a reported polling result and should not be interpreted as an independent determination of the causes of inflation.

articles.title: AP-NORC Poll Finds Widespread Concern About US Living Costs
articles.content: An AP-NORC poll conducted from September 24 to 28 among 2,140 US adults found that 65% said Trump's policies were responsible for persistently high prices. The poll also found low approval ratings for his handling of living costs and the economy. These figures describe public opinion measured in the survey and do not independently establish the causes of inflation.

articles.title: Canada Designates Pacific Link Pipeline as Project of National Interest
articles.content: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has formally designated the proposed Pacific Link oil pipeline as a project of national interest under the Building Canada Act. The proposed pipeline would transport roughly 1 million barrels of crude oil per day from Alberta towards Canada's west coast. Canada and Alberta will share equal ownership, while Indigenous communities are being offered a minimum 10% ownership interest financed through Indigenous loan guarantee programmes. Federal conditions and consultations are expected to continue through 2027.

articles.title: North Korea Launches Ballistic Missile Towards East Sea
articles.content: South Korea's military said North Korea launched a ballistic missile from the Wonsan area at around 6:30 a.m. on Saturday. The missile travelled more than 700 kilometres before landing at sea. South Korean and US authorities are analysing the exact specifications. The launch comes amid heightened tensions following a September 21 landmine blast near the inter-Korean border that injured three South Korean soldiers.

articles.title: China Remains Focused on Energy, Technology and Regional Security
articles.content: China continues to focus on energy security, advanced technology and its strategic position in Asia. The wider US-China relationship remains under close observation following recent high-level contacts between Washington and Beijing. Taiwan, the South China Sea, technology supply chains and energy security remain important issues in the regional environment.

articles.title: Australia Inflation Rises to 4.0%
articles.content: Australia's Consumer Price Index rose 4.0% in the 12 months to August 2026, up from 3.5% in July, according to the Australian Bureau of Statistics. The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate to 4.60% on 30 September. Higher household costs, including housing and energy-related expenses, remain important factors for Australian consumers.

articles.title: Nigeria Economy Grows 4.43% in Q2 2026
articles.content: Nigeria's real GDP grew by 4.43% year-on-year in the second quarter of 2026, according to the National Bureau of Statistics. Growth improved from 3.89% in the first quarter. Services remained the largest contributor to economic output, while agriculture and the oil sector also recorded growth. The figures show economic expansion, although household living standards can be affected by inflation, fuel costs and other cost-of-living pressures.

articles.title: Nigeria Continues to Navigate Energy and Cost-of-Living Pressures
articles.content: Nigeria remains exposed to international energy prices despite improvements in domestic economic activity and refining capacity. Changes in global oil prices can influence transport, food production, electricity generation and household expenses. For an oil-producing country, higher international prices can also increase export revenues, creating a complex balance between government income and consumer costs.

articles.title: Pew Finds Growing Concern About Social Media and Political Division
articles.content: A new Pew Research Center survey covering 37 countries found that a median of 79% of adults said internet and social media access has made people easier to manipulate with false information and rumours, while 68% said it has made people more divided in their political opinions. At the same time, 77% said social media and the internet have made people more informed about current events and 60% said they have given people a more meaningful voice in politics. The findings underline both the benefits and risks of digital information.

morningSummary.title: Today's Global Picture
morningSummary.content: Energy security dominates the global agenda as the G7 moves to release emergency oil and fuel reserves. France is dealing with a rapidly expanding student protest movement, while Europe continues to face energy and inflation pressures. The UK has reported stronger-than-expected Q2 growth. Canada is moving ahead with the Pacific Link pipeline. North Korea has launched another ballistic missile, Australia is dealing with higher inflation, and Nigeria continues to balance economic growth with cost-of-living pressures.

bigQuestion: With energy prices affecting countries across the world, how can governments protect ordinary people from rising living costs without creating new economic problems?
